backlog.spec: Change the SLSQP variables so that each radius is r = s^2, with s as the optimised variable and bounds on s of [0, 0.5]. Constraints become (distance squared compared to (s_i + s_j)^2) or equivalently keep the existing distance constraint with r replaced by s*s. Map the result back to radii before repair. The constraint remains smooth at zero radius, and this removes the active bound on radii. Keep all other settings and the restart logic unchanged.
backlog.title: Squared-radius reparametrisation

backlog.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (2) Add a constant PERTURB_ITER = 100 and use it as SLSQP maxiter when start is not None (MAX_ITER = 200 stays for fresh starts). A perturbed copy of a good packing is close to a local optimum, so shorter runs should allow about twice as many perturbation trials in the same time.
backlog.title: Maximin starts and shorter SLSQP runs in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: Two changes. (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the initial centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (2) When start is not None, make SLSQP cheaper by restricting the pair constraints: after building the perturbed x0, keep only pairs (i, j) whose centre distance in x0 is below 0.45, and keep all pairs involving any relocated circle (the idx circles). Build iu from this subset. Wall and radius constraints stay complete. _repair already checks all pairs, so a dropped pair that ends up overlapping is still fixed before the result is compared. This should cut the constraint count by more than half and allow more perturbation trials.
backlog.title: Maximin starts and near-pair constraints in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 pick the centres by farthest-point sampling from 400 uniform candidates in [0.05, 0.95]^2 (first point random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen points). For these starts set each initial radius to 0.48 times the distance to the nearest other centre, capped by the distance to the nearest wall, instead of the constant INIT_RADIUS, so SLSQP starts from a feasible and already fairly dense packing with unequal radii. The other half of the fresh starts and the whole perturbation phase stay as they are.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with feasible nearest-neighbour radii

backlog.spec: Combine two replicated winners. Fresh starts: half use maximin centres (best of 400 candidates). Perturbation phase: replace the 2-3 circle move with shaking all centres by normal noise sd 0.05, running SLSQP with maxiter=60 from there, then continuing the usual maxiter to convergence only if the 60-iteration result is within 0.01 of the best sum. Accept if the repaired sum improves.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with shake-all perturbation

backlog.spec: Use maximin starts for half of fresh restarts, shift the restart share from 30% to 20% of the budget, and in the perturbation phase use a mix: 50% shake-all centres with sd drawn uniformly from [0.03,0.07] followed by SLSQP, 50% the existing move of 2-3 circles. Accept if better.
backlog.title: Maximin starts, 20% restart share, shake perturbation

backlog.spec: Add maximin starts for half of the fresh starts (400 candidates uniform in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, random first pick, then greedily add the candidate with the largest min-distance to the chosen points). In the fresh-start phase only, run SLSQP in two stages. Stage 1 uses maxiter=40. Repair a copy of the stage-1 result; if its radii sum is below best_sum - 0.03, return the repaired stage-1 result without continuing. Otherwise continue SLSQP from the stage-1 x for 160 more iterations. To do this, give _solve_once a threshold argument (None in the perturbation phase) and keep the final repair in solve as it is.
backlog.title: Early abort of weak restarts with maximin starts

backlog.spec: After _repair, the radii are often shrunk more than needed. Add a final step: find the largest factor f in [1, 1.05] such that the radii multiplied by f still give a valid packing, using bisection with 30 steps. Validity means every circle is inside the square and every pair satisfies d >= r_i + r_j, computed exactly. Apply the largest valid f, then subtract SHRINK as before. Only accept the scaled radii if the check passes, so the output stays valid.
backlog.title: Scale-recovery bisection after repair

backlog.spec: Change only fresh starts (start is None in _solve_once), with three equally likely types. (a) Uniform as now. (b) Maximin: farthest-point sampling of n centres from 400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2 (first random, then repeatedly the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set). (c) Symmetric maximin: farthest-point sample 13 centres from 200 candidates in [INIT_LOW, 0.47] x [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW], mirror them through x = 0.5 to get the other 13, then add normal jitter of sd 0.005 to all centres to break exact symmetry. Initial radii stay INIT_RADIUS. Leave the perturbation phase untouched.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with mirror-symmetric variant

backlog.spec: Combine the two replicated winners (slot 34 and slot 31). (1) In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 build the initial centres by farthest-point sampling instead of uniform: draw 400 candidate points uniformly in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, pick the first at random, then repeatedly add the candidate whose minimum distance to the already chosen points is largest, until n are chosen; radii stay INIT_RADIUS. (2) In the perturbation phase (start is not None) add a third move with probability 1/3: add normal noise of sd 0.05 to ALL centres (clip to [0.01, 0.99]), run SLSQP with maxiter 60, and only if the resulting radius sum is within 0.02 of the best sum continue from that point with another 140 iterations; otherwise return the 60-iteration result. The other two moves (relocate 2-3 circles, jitter sd 0.02) share the remaining 2/3 equally. Keep everything else, including _repair and the 30% restart share.
backlog.title: Maximin starts plus shake-all perturbation move

backlog.spec: For fresh starts (start None), always use maximin centres: take 400 candidates from rng.uniform(0.05, 0.95, (400,2)), pick a random first candidate, then greedily add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen points until there are n. Set each initial radius to min(0.5 * distance to its nearest other centre, distance to the nearest wall) * 0.9, so the start is almost feasible and the circles already have different sizes. Feed that to SLSQP as x0. The perturbation phase is unchanged.
backlog.title: Maximin starts with radius-growth initial radii

backlog.spec: Slot 34 used maximin centres for half of the fresh starts; test using them for all. In _solve_once, when start is None, always build centres by farthest-point sampling: draw m uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, where m is drawn per start from {60, 150, 400} (fewer candidates gives a more irregular layout, more gives a near-uniform one), choose the first point at random and then repeatedly add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set until n are chosen. Then add normal jitter of sd 0.01 to the centres. Initial radii stay INIT_RADIUS. Nothing else changes.
backlog.title: Maximin for every fresh start, with varied candidate count

backlog.spec: In _solve_once, when start is None, with probability 0.5 (rng.random()<0.5) replace the uniform initial centres with farthest-point (maximin) centres. Draw 400 candidate points with rng.uniform(INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW, (400,2)). Pick the first point at random with rng.integers. Then n-1 times, add the candidate whose minimum distance to the points already chosen is largest (keep a running min-distance array and update it with np.minimum after each pick). Radii stay at INIT_RADIUS. Change nothing else. This reproduces slot 34, which scored -2.6342/-2.6337 over 2 runs against the incumbent's -2.6313, so it should be confirmed and adopted.
backlog.title: Re-run maximin starts (slot 34) as the new base

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, identify rattlers in the current best packing: circles with fewer than 2 contacts, where a contact means the gap between two circles or between a circle and a wall is below 1e-6. With probability 1/2 per perturbation, remove one rattler chosen at random and reinsert it at the point with the largest clearance, found by checking 2000 random candidates against all circles and walls. Set its radius to that clearance, then run the existing SLSQP polish and repair. If there are no rattlers, use the smallest circle instead.
backlog.title: Rattler reinsertion into the largest hole

backlog.spec: In solve, during the perturbation phase, keep a 'current' packing separate from 'best'. Perturb the current packing, not the best one. Accept the new packing as current if its sum is above current_sum - T, where T decays linearly from 0.004 at the start of the perturbation phase to 0 at the end of the time budget; always update best when a new sum exceeds best_sum. If 15 perturbations in a row fail to improve best, reset current to best. Everything else, including the moves themselves, stays the same.
backlog.title: Annealed acceptance in the perturbation phase

backlog.spec: In the perturbation phase, run two independent chains from the best restart packing, each with its own rng stream derived from seed (for example seed+1 and seed+2). Each chain uses the existing shake-and-polish move. Split the remaining time evenly between chains by alternating one step at a time, and return the best packing across both chains. This adds diversity to the local search without changing the moves.
backlog.title: Two independent perturbation chains

backlog.spec: For half of fresh starts, choose maximin centres (best of 400 candidates), then set initial radii by greedy growth: r_i = min(wall distance, half of the distance to the nearest other centre) * 0.9. SLSQP then starts from a nearly feasible, varied-radius configuration.
backlog.title: Radius-growth maximin start

backlog.spec: Make half of fresh random starts use farthest-point (maximin) sampled centres: for each start, pick each new centre as the best of 400 random candidates in [0.03,0.97]^2 maximising the minimum distance to already chosen centres, with initial radii 0.05. Keep the 30% restart then perturbation structure unchanged. This is the slot 34 idea with a replicate-ready clean implementation.
backlog.title: Maximin starts plus 30% restart share base

backlog.spec: Split fresh starts (start None) into three types, chosen with rng.random(): with probability 0.4 use maximin centres (400 candidates uniform in [0.1,0.9]^2, random first pick, then greedily add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen set); with probability 0.3 put 12 circles in a jittered perimeter ring (parameter t uniform around the square boundary, at distance uniform(0.03,0.12) inward from the wall) and the other 14 uniform in [0.2,0.8]^2; otherwise use the current uniform start. All radii start at INIT_RADIUS. The perturbation phase is unchanged.
backlog.title: Maximin starts plus perimeter-ring starts mix

backlog.spec: Implement three changes together. (1) Fresh starts: with probability 0.5 use farthest-point sampling (400 uniform candidates in [INIT_LOW, 1-INIT_LOW]^2, first point random, then repeatedly add the candidate with the largest minimum distance to the chosen points) for all n centres. (2) With probability 0.25 use 12 perimeter circles (3 per wall, evenly spaced with sd 0.03 jitter, distance uniform(0.03, 0.12) from the wall) plus 14 interior centres drawn uniformly in [0.2, 0.8]^2; the remaining 0.25 stay uniform as now. (3) In the perturbation phase, one third of the moves add normal noise of sd 0.05 to all centres (clip to [0.01, 0.99]) and run SLSQP at the normal MAX_ITER; the other two moves split the rest equally. Keep the 30% restart share, _repair and all constants.
backlog.title: Full combination: maximin, ring and shake-all

memo:
Helped: only slot 7 (30% of time on random restarts, then perturbing the best packing by moving 2-3 circles): -2.6310/-2.6316, incumbent -2.6313 over 2 runs. Slot 6 (50% share) was +0.0005 vs incumbent. Slot 29 (15% share) scored -2.6322, one run, within noise (sd 0.0023).
Not helpful: init tweaks (0, 2), analytic gradients (3), screening/looser tolerances (1, 10), LP refit (5), pair-restricted continuation (4), TIME_FRACTION 0.9 (9), MAX_ITER 500 (12), final polish (13), wall-hugging starts (20), elite pool (19), later perturbation variants (22, 25, 26, 28).
Replicated: slot 34 (maximin starts) scored -2.6342/-2.6337 and slot 31 (shake all centres) scored -2.6337/-2.6327. Both beat the incumbent's -2.6313 on two runs, yet were marked reject. Recheck that decision.
Singles that looked slightly better: 17 (-2.6330), 24 (-2.6327), 15 (-2.6324), 23 (-2.6324), 30 (-2.6323). Slot 27's -2.6300 suggests the symmetric-start gain is noise.
Next: make slot 34 the base. Combine it with the slot 31 shake and the slot 24 ring. Then tune the restart share (15-30%). Avoid more perturbation variants.
